newsitem.title: USA: Treasury's Summers urges African trade integration.
newsitem.headline: Treasury's Summers urges African trade integration.

text.p: The Clinton administration hopes that opening U.S. markets to more South African trade will add momemtum to its efforts to integrate more closely with neighboring Africa economies, Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Thursday.

In a speech prepared for delivery in New York to a seminar at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, Summers said greater liberalization of investment rules by the South African government would add to its appeal as a place in which to invest.
A text was issued in Washington.

"With the NAFTA example in mind, I'm convinced that the South African Development Community has trememndous potential to benefit all parties, despite substantial differences in the level of development among the SADC members," Summers said.
He added it could also serve as "an anchor" for South Africa regarding its own trade reforms, enabling the government to resist urgings from domestic producers for special protection for their goods.
The Clinton administration has proposed a program called Partnership for Economic Growth and Opportunity in Africa that is partly aimed at fostering more investment in Africa.
Summers said South Africa should become "the driving-force of a region-wide recovery," with its most important contribution to that process being the acceleration of its own growth.

He acknowledged that South Africa faces tough political and economic choices to reform its labor markets, but said it could do more immediately to encourage education and to reduce trade and investment restrictions.
He noted that only 18 percent of South Africa's adult population was literate and said research shows that no country has ever taken off economically with a literacy rate under 50 percent.
